name: Cloudflare Pages
summary: Git-connected hosting for static and full-stack sites: every push is built and deployed to Cloudflare’s CDN with its own preview URL, and a `functions/` folder becomes Workers behind the site. Cloudflare now tells new projects to use Workers instead.
intro: You connect a GitHub or GitLab repository, pick a framework preset or build command, and Pages builds every push (up to 20 minutes per build, 500 builds a month on the Free plan) and uploads the output to Cloudflare’s network. The production branch updates `<project>.pages.dev` and any custom domains; every other branch and pull request gets its own preview URL, posted back to the pull request, and any deployment can be rolled back instantly. Assets stay in the CDN cache, including Tiered Cache, until the next deployment, and requests for them are free and unlimited. `_headers` and `_redirects` files set headers and up to 2,100 redirects without code, and a missing top-level `404.html` turns on single-page-app routing.

Pages Functions add a backend: a file such as `functions/api/users/[id].ts` exporting `onRequest` becomes a route, running as a Worker with the same bindings to KV, D1, R2 and Workers AI and billed as Workers requests. The catch is strategic. Since Workers gained free static assets, framework support and Git builds in 2024 and 2025, Cloudflare has said Pages “will continue to be supported” but that all its investment and feature work goes to Workers; the Pages docs open with “Start new projects with Workers” and link a migration guide.
strengths: Git push to deploy with no CI to configure: builds, status checks and a preview URL for every branch and pull request
Static asset requests are free and unlimited, served from Cloudflare’s cache until the next deploy
Unlimited preview deployments and instant rollbacks to any earlier production deployment
Custom domains can live outside Cloudflare-managed zones (via CNAME), which Workers doesn’t support
limits: No new features: Cloudflare puts its investment into Workers, which already has things Pages lacks, such as gradual deployments, Cron Triggers, queue consumers, Workers Logs and the Vite plugin
Durable Objects need a separate Worker, and Functions can’t consume queues or use Cron Triggers
25 MiB per file, 20,000 files per site on Free (100,000 on paid plans) and 100 projects per account, rarely increased
Builds time out after 20 minutes, and the Free plan runs one build at a time

story: In 2020, a frontend developer who wanted a site online had to stitch together hosting and a CI system configured in YAML, waiting minutes per build and rerunning the same build hoping for a different result. On December 17, 2020, Rita Kozlov announced Cloudflare Pages as “a fast, secure and free way to build and host your JAMstack sites”: select a repository and framework, `git push`, and Cloudflare builds and deploys to its network, with a unique preview URL for each commit and unlimited collaborators for free. It became generally available on April 12, 2021, after thousands of developers deployed over ten thousand projects in the beta.

The launch post already promised a backend built on Workers. Pages Functions followed in November 2021, routing files in a `functions/` folder to what are, in Cloudflare’s words, Workers “in disguise”, and became generally available in November 2022. But the two products kept growing into each other, and in May 2023 Cloudflare announced it would converge Pages and Workers to end the “decision paralysis” of choosing between them.

The convergence happened inside Workers. Static assets on Workers entered beta in September 2024, and in April 2025 Cloudflare added `_headers` and `_redirects`, Git builds and preview URLs to Workers, telling developers to start with Workers: Pages would stay supported, but new investment would go to Workers. The Pages docs now carry the same advice and a migration guide.

choices.why: Instead of asking frontend developers to configure CI, Pages builds and deploys on every push, so their existing workflow is the deployment pipeline.

choices.choice: A preview URL for every commit
choices.why: Reviewers, designers and product managers can look at a running version of a change without pulling the branch and running it locally.
Rather than build a second compute platform, Pages reused Workers for its backend, so Functions get the same runtime, scale and bindings.

timeline.text: Announced on December 17 as free Jamstack hosting with Git builds and preview URLs
Pages goes full stack with Functions (beta) and GitLab support in November
Pages Functions generally available in November
Cloudflare announces Pages and Workers will converge, in May
Workers gains Pages’ features; Cloudflare says to start new projects on Workers
